thread:
pagerduty: INCIDENT ALERT — high CPU OOM rate on inference-preproc (service: runtime-tokenize). Trigger: 5x POD OOM in 10m. Priority: P1. Paging maria (oncall).

ops-bot: automated metrics snapshot: preproc cpu usage across pool 'rp-tokenize-prod' jumped from 25% -> 95% over 3m; pod restarts=6; node flaps detected in gke-us-west1-3. Suspected heavy prompt bursts with large token counts. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/rp-tokenize-prod

maria: on it. I'm pulling logs now. Anyone oncall overlap? @alex are you available to assist?

alex: here, awake. I'll take network/routing mitigation. Maria, can you confirm whether this is one customer burst or many small ones?

maria: quick grep of logs shows many unique client_ids but a handful (~4) account_ids contributing ~60% of tokens in the spike. Likely a customer-side job running a prompt-sweep.

jing: possible vector: aggressive client-side pre-tokenization + long system prompts hitting our tokenize worker. We saw similar behavior with the normalize/tokenize worker when unicode normalization path fell back to slow codepath. Check for repeated backtracking in tokenizer (esp. heavy regex).

maria: attaching a snippet of pod logs from pod runtime-tokenize-7b8f: ```
W 11:03:12 TokenizeWorker pid=1 cpu=98% ctx=tokenize_handler heavy prompt size=1.2M chars
E 11:03:12 runtime: alloc did not return - kernel OOM? process killed
I 11:03:13 kubelet: container "tokenizer" exited with code 137
```

sam: oncall-sre here. Recommending immediate mitigations: 1) scale up replica count for tokenizers to spread short-term load, 2) apply an ingress request-size limit to drop >500k char prompts, 3) add emergency rate-limit for the 4 customer IDs (temp block).

alex: implementing ingress rule now. Pushing a temporary Envoy filter to reject large bodies >500k chars and attach header x-rate-emergency: true. Command: ```kubectl patch envoyfilter emergency-rate --type merge -p '{"spec": {"filters": [{"name": "envoy.filters.http.lua","typed_config": {"inline_code":"-- check content-length; reject if >524288"}}]}}' -n redwood-runtime```

maria: scaling tokenizers up (hotfix): ```kubectl scale deployment runtime-tokenize --replicas=12 -n redwood-runtime``` will take ~90s to spin up. Also cordoning the worst-flapping node gke-us-west1-3b to prevent further pod churn. ```kubectl cordon gke-us-west1-3b```

ops-bot: autoscaler activity: nodepool 'tokenize-np' queued scale up, adding 3 nodes. Expected capacity in ~4m.

jing: for longer-term: if unicode-normalize fallback triggers expensive NFKC on huge inputs we should short-circuit early and return 413 or normalized failure. For now can we toggle the fast-path flag?

maria: located the fast_path flag in config map runtime-tokenizer-config. Patching to enable strict-length early-exit: ```kubectl set env deployment/runtime-tokenize EARLY_EXIT_MAX_CHARS=524288 -n redwood-runtime```

sam: also please add temporary placement policy so heavy customer requests go to dedicated smaller-vec pool (reduces noisy-neighboring). Alex, can you do routing?

alex: routing rule added: requests with x-customer-id in [acct-42, acct-71, acct-909, acct-17] get routed to dedicated-pool-tokenize (quota=reserved). I also added fallback to lightweight-bypass-tokenizer for customers that opt-in.

maria: after scaling + ingress + env toggle, restart churn reduced. New logs: ```
I 11:07:42 TokenizeWorker pid=1 cpu=35% handle normal prompt.
I 11:07:50 kubelet: started container "tokenizer" for runtime-tokenize-2cd4
```

ops-bot: pod restarts/down events dropped from 6 -> 1 in last 5m. Node gke-us-west1-3 still shows kernel OOM messages; we've marked it unschedulable.

sam: customer impact update: partial degradation for large-batched prompts; latency for normal prompts recovered to SLO. Standup notice: affected accounts were rate-limited (temporary) and routed. No data loss. Potentially one paying customer will need follow-up.

jing: found a stacktrace in the slow path: ```
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
 at com.redwood.tokenize.RegexNormalizer.normalize(RegexNormalizer.java:142)
 at com.redwood.tokenize.TokenizeService.handle(TokenizeService.java:89)
```

maria: agreed. Filing follow-up tickets: 1) short-term: add strict prompt-size validation and fail-fast (owner: runtime-team) 2) mid-term: implement streaming normalization (owner: eng-ml) 3) infra: harden node autoscaler thresholds and cordon policies (owner: eng-infra).

alex: paging update to product/sales for impacted accounts and offering to roll back rate-limit in exchange for cooperative throttling on their side. I'll draft message.

maria: handing off to sam for next shift (sam is taking over). Sam, I'm leaving the thread with mitigation steps recorded. Summary pinned to incident channel and I'll start a linked postmortem once we stabilize.

sam: taking over. Thanks Maria. I'll monitor for 30m then transition to SRE queue. Posting triage checklist: root cause suspected: unbounded heavy prompts hitting a slow unicode-normalizer path -> CPU OOM -> container exit 137 -> repeated pod restarts -> node kernel OOMs -> node flaps.

pagerduty: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied. Severity reduced to P2. Followups required: customer outreach, streaming-normalizer RFC, ingress validation rule as permanent config.

maria: final note: keep the emergency ingress rule and EARLY_EXIT_MAX_CHARS flag until followups are complete. Will attach logs and kubectl outputs to postmortem. :heavy_check_mark:

sam: acknowledged. Closing active paging. Will draft incident report and link here when ready. :memo:
